mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increase and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a single month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to concerns about consumer spending and economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increase and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over two months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which often leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as it reflects broader economic weakness.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between HOUST decline and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a single month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as it reflects increased economic activity and potential corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increase and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same period, it signals a strengthening consumer demand and labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint correlation between RSAFS increase, UNRATE decrease, and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs per month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as it reflects increased economic activity and potential corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in periods of strong job growth are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4%, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: inflationary period with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint correlation between CPIAUCSL increase, high FEDFUNDS, and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
